title: Expose a navigation location map for use in CSS

labels.name: agenda+
labels.description: To be discussed at a triage meeting

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

[css-navigation-1](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-navigation-1/) allows styling the document based on the current navigation. See [explainer](https://github.com/WICG/declarative-partial-updates/blob/main/route-matching-explainer.md) for a full set of use cases etc.

### What solutions exist today?

The current spec allows [using CSS to declare navigation locations](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-navigation-1/#url-pattern-function). However, this is unacceptable from the point of view of security - letting stylesheets sniff the full document URL with RegExp/wildcards would exfiltrate the document URL in new ways.

### How would you solve it?

See https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14266#issuecomment-6196149652

Proposing to copy the `importmap` model and have a `locationmap` - a script type that contains JSON, which maps a location name to a [`URLPatternInit`](https://urlpattern.spec.whatwg.org/#dictdef-urlpatterninit):

```html
<script type=locationmap src="locations.json"></script>
```
`locations.json`:
```json
{ "home" : "/", "item": { "pathname": "/item/:id" } }
```

```html
<!-- or inline -->
<script type=locationmap>
{ 
  "locations": {
     "home" : "/", 
     "item": { pathname: "/item/:id"}
  }
}
</script>
```





### Anything else?

Some details:
- Use script and not link because it can be inline if desired.
- JSON and not CSS/custom, to stay consistent and simple and not tie to being CSS-specific.
- For styling navigations, the map is only read once at the start of a navigation and then frozen throughout the navigation, so adding/removing those scripts generally doesn't cause style invalidation. An exception is the `:link-to` pseudo-class but that's generally cheaper to invalidate.
- Apart from this, mutability should work the same way as `importmap`.
